cards.explanation: The answer is False. Asaph opens with a shout, not a hush: "Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob." (Psalm 81:1) Joyful NOISE is what the text says, friends. I think a librarian would have needed a minute with this one.

The answer is at the New Moon and the full moon. Asaph says, "Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast." (Psalm 81:3) The horn goes with the calendar, friends. Moon in the sky, horn in the air.

The answer is that God made it a statute for Israel. Asaph says, "For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob." (Psalm 81:4) A statute is something God set in place. So the singing and the horn aren't random, friends. They come from His ordinance.

The answer is Egypt. The psalm says God ordained it as a testimony for Joseph "…when he went out over the land of Egypt…" (Psalm 81:5) Egypt is the land the verse names, friends. It's right there in the middle of the line.

The answer is that He freed them from it. God says, "I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket." (Psalm 81:6) He didn't tweak the load or help them carry it better, friends. He took it off.
The answer is rescued. God says, "You called out in distress, and I rescued you…" (Psalm 81:7) They called, and He answered with a rescue, friends. Hearing that gives me all the warm feelings.

The answer is True. God says, "I answered you from the cloud of thunder…" (Psalm 81:7) Right before that, He says, "You called out in distress, and I rescued you…" His answer came with thunder, friends, and I think that's one answer nobody had to ask Him to repeat.

The answer is that He tested His people. God says, "I tested you at the waters of Meribah." (Psalm 81:7) That's all the psalm says about it here, friends. It's a short line, but it carries a whole memory.
The answer is True. God says, "O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!" (Psalm 81:8) That's a wish, friends, and it shows what He wants for His people. I'd say that's a heart worth hearing.
The answer is a strange god. God says, "There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god." (Psalm 81:9) He says it plainly, friends. No other god belongs among them.

The answer is False. God says, "But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me." (Psalm 81:11) The offer was there, friends, and the listening wasn't. I think this verse is a heavy one.

The answer is that God gives them up to their stubborn hearts. He says, "So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices." (Psalm 81:12) Just before that, He says, "But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me." (Psalm 81:11) That's a serious line, friends, and I think it's one to slow down for.

The answer is that He'd subdue their enemies. God says, "…how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!" (Psalm 81:14) Notice the "how soon," friends. He says it would come quickly.
The answer is False. God says, "Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience…" (Psalm 81:15) Feigning means pretending, friends. The obedience would be an act, not the real thing.
The answer is the finest wheat. God says, "But I would feed you the finest wheat…" (Psalm 81:16) The finest, friends, not leftovers or scraps. I'm a cookie guy, so I get excited about good grain.
